His unprecedented 12-month clean sweep may be over following a crushing 10-4 defeat by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam and a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix , but he can still qualify for next month's Players Championship Finals. The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay. messages.text: How does Arteta turn champions into serial winners?

metadata.summary: When Mikel Arteta signed his last Arsenal contract in September 2024, his quest to bring major silverware back to the club was ongoing. Two years later, he signs his new one after leading them to a long-awaited Premier League title.
metadata.content: Mikel Arteta to begin new era at Arsenal as club eye Premier League dominance and Champions League success | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Mikel Arteta to begin new era at Arsenal as club eye Premier League dominance and Champions League success Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract as Arsenal manager; Gunners boss has overseen a total transformation of the club since his arrival in 2019, so can he now achieve greatness and become only fifth manager in win multiple Premier League titles? Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Wednesday 7 October 2026 11:57, UK Image: Mikel Arteta took over as Arsenal head coach in 2019 When Mikel Arteta signed his last Arsenal contract in September 2024, his quest to bring major silverware back to the club was ongoing. Two years later, he signs his new one after leading them to a long-awaited Premier League title. His task now is to turn champions into serial winners. Arteta has overseen a total transformation of the club since his appointment in 2019. Arsenal, 10th in the Premier League table when he took over, were in a state of drift. Now, they are re-established among Europe's elite, unrecognisable in all departments. Arteta has joined a select group of 13 managers to have won the Premier League. He now has the chance to join an even smaller group, made up of only Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger, by winning it more than once.
